provenance.pipeline: satsuki v1 (v1.0.1 editorial re-edit: usage-note reshaping corpus-wide, lane discrimination for same-surface families, against prompts/style.md)

patterns.usage_note: Names the goal an action serves: a non-past volitional verb or a noun plus の states the aim, and the main clause is the deliberate action taken to reach it (合格するために勉強する, 家族のために働く). The sibling entry is the causal ため, which gives the reason something happened (大雪のため中止). ために modifies a verb and ための a following noun (留学するための資金); where the main clause reports a cost or an evaluation rather than a chosen action, のに is used.

examples.ruby: 留学[りゅうがく]するために毎朝[まいあさ]英語[えいご]を勉強[べんきょう]している。
examples.english: I study English every morning so that I can go study abroad.

examples.ruby: 試合[しあい]に勝[か]つための練習[れんしゅう]を一年[いちねん]続[つづ]けた。
examples.english: We kept up a year of training aimed at winning the match.

examples.ruby: 早[はや]く起[お]きるための工夫[くふう]をいろいろ試[ため]した。
examples.english: I tried all sorts of tricks for getting up early.

patterns.usage_note: Names the use something is judged for: the main clause gives an evaluation, a requirement, or a cost (調べるのに便利だ, 歩くのに二十分かかる). ために states the aim a deliberate action serves instead. んに is a relaxed, regional contraction of のに. The concessive のに "even though" is a different pattern, taking a clause on both sides and な after na-adjectives and nouns (静かなのに).

examples.ruby: このアプリは乗[の]り換[か]えを調[しら]べるのに便利[べんり]だ。
examples.english: This app is handy for looking up transfers.

examples.ruby: ここから駅[えき]まで歩[ある]くのに二十分[にじゅっぷん]かかる。
examples.english: It takes twenty minutes to walk from here to the station.

examples.ruby: この鍋[なべ]はカレーを作[つく]るのにちょうどいい大[おお]きさだ。
examples.english: This pot is just the right size for making curry.
